heard: A secret radioactive clock is bolted to the side of Voyager. In 1977, NASA launched twin robotic probes into space, carrying identical gold-plated phonograph records as time capsules for extraterrestrial civilizations. The recordings hold natural sounds of thunder and whale songs, spoken greetings in 55 languages, and Andruin's brainwaves while falling in love. Committee Chair Carl Sagan even added a pulsar map, locating our solar system relative to 14 pulsars. To protect the records, engineers fitted an aluminum cover electroplated with an ultra-pure sample of uranium-238, which has a half-life of approximately 4.5 billion years. By measuring that radioactive decay, any finder can read the record's precise age, deciphering how long ago Earth sent its cosmic message.
